summary: Douglas Osto specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned a Master's from the University of Washington and a PhD from SOAS under Ulrich Pagel. Around 2005, he became Senior Lecturer and Programme Coordinator at Massey University.

Douglas S. Duckworth is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He completed his BA at James Madison University, and an MA and PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, later serving as Assistant Professor at East Tennessee State University (~2007–2013).
Dragana Majhen works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Manitoba, completing a Master's degree under the supervision of Albert Welter (attested 2010).

Dragomir Dimitrov is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA and a PhD under Michael Hahn at the University of Marburg, where he held posts attested in 2002 and 2020, alongside a post at the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project.
Drolma is a Tibetologist who earned an M.Phil. in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo under the supervision of Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008).
Dror Burstein is a scholar working in Buddhist studies and other fields. He taught literature at Tel Aviv University around 2011 and held a post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem in 2014.

Duncan Ryūken Williams specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. After studying at Reed College and Harvard University, he served as Assistant Professor of East Asian Buddhism at UC Irvine (~1999–2006) and held a post at UC Berkeley (~2006–2011).
Dung Ngoc Duong is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed a PhD at Boston University under the supervision of Malcolm David Eckel (attested 2001).

Dungkar Lozang Trinlé was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Gyuto Monastery. He served as a full professor at Minzu University of China (~1959–1965), Director of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences, and taught at Tibet University (~1985–1997).
Durga Prasad Dikshit is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He studied under R. K. Dikshit, Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi, and doctoral supervisor Baij Nath Puri.

Durgamohan Bhattacharyya (1899–1965) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Scottish Church College, Vidyasagar College, and the University of Calcutta, where he later held an academic post.

Dwijendra Nath Shukla was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He earned a D.Litt. from the University of Lucknow under K. A. Subramania Iyer and held a post at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University (attested 1958).
Dylan Esler specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA from SOAS University of London and a PhD from KU Leuven, where he also held a post as a research scholar.

Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, and served as professor of Buddhist philosophy at Naropa University in 1990.

Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Columbia University, and served as director of Nitartha Institute (~1996) and Kamalashila Institute (attested 2013).

Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Sakya College and SOAS University of London, learning from teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, and Sakya Trizin.

Dörte Kamarid works in Tibetology and Indology. She studied at the University of Vienna, Savitribai Phule Pune University, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, completing an MA supervised by Helmut Tauscher.

E. Gene Smith (1936–2010) was a Tibetologist who studied at several institutions, including the University of Washington under Turrell V. Wylie. He worked at the Library of Congress (~1968–1997) and directed the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (~1999–2010).
E. H. Johnston (1885–1942) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Arthur Anthony Macdonell and served as a professor at the University of Oxford (attested 1940).

E. Michael Mendelson (1928–2024) was a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He pursued his education at King's College, the University of Cambridge, the University of Paris, and the University of Chicago (~1953–1956).
